findings.text: Within three short paragraphs a newcomer learns what Athena is, what a 'study' is, and why this page exists. That covers the 'what is it' question well.
findings.source: "Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository."

findings.text: A clear next step is linked at the top, so a newcomer who doesn't care about firstmate can jump straight to it.
findings.source: "Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself."

findings.text: Nothing else on the page backs up these selling points. The only Athena output shown is this study, so 'why it matters' rests on one sentence and on the reader working through the firstmate material.
findings.source: "It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost."

findings.text: Almost all of the page covers firstmate's internals (exit codes, worktree places, teardown rules), even though the URL is Athena's site. A newcomer who came to learn about Athena has to work out alone which parts concern them.
findings.source: Headings: States of a piece of work, Counters, Transitions, Why it is built this way, Glossary, Claims and sources

findings.text: The install step gives no clone command and no prerequisites (for example a Rust toolchain or model API keys). It also doesn't say which repository `athena ask` acts on or what the user gets back, so a newcomer may get stuck.
findings.source: Next steps: "Install Athena from a checkout of its repository: ./setup.sh" and "Try it with a one-line request: athena ask "add a changelog""

findings.text: Several terms are used but never defined in 'Words used first' or the Glossary: endpoint, brief, captain call, merge authority. The Glossary defines 'stale wake' only circularly ('A wake after which…').
findings.source: t8 card: "a secondmate re-reads its pin and needs none, and a secondmate with no endpoint is recovered by the spawn script instead"; c3: "before it renders a brief or creates an endpoint"

findings.text: Being frank about gaps is good for trust. But this hedge and others like it ('The cited text states no…') come up again and again, alongside the exit-75 and places rules repeated four or five times. That makes the page longer and harder for a first-time reader.
findings.source: "The cited instruction does not say what makes work in scope, so this page gives no test for it."

findings.text: The page states plainly that nothing was run. This helps a reader judge how far to trust what it says.
findings.source: Limits of this study: "This study read the pinned tree only... no failure or retry edge was observed; every claim is marked read."

findings.text: The closing section and the footer point to an internal folder without saying where it is or why a reader would want it, so they mean nothing to a newcomer.
findings.source: About this page: "is the name of the folder under studies/ that holds the data this page is generated from."
